probe: DEC-9 — is the DS table-free radix cold/warm SELECTION divergence fixable on the DS side?
op_point: GLM-5.1-FP8, TP=8, fp8_e4m3, page 64, mem 0.8, max-running 64, EAGER (--disable-cuda-graph), base DS config (no removed fields), score_reduce_dtype default = bf16

Q1_determinism_control.setup: radix OFF (--disable-radix-cache), selection_capture only, NO new code; two FRESH identical requests (both cached_tokens=0)
Q1_determinism_control.verdict: BIT-IDENTICAL — two fresh requests select the identical top-2048 on every rank (8) x DS layer (78). DS selection is DETERMINISTIC given inputs. The R24 cold/warm flip is therefore RADIX-SPECIFIC (the cached-decode path differs from a fresh-decode), NOT general run-to-run non-determinism. This also proves the cross-TP bf16 reduce is deterministic given identical inputs.

Q2_score_trace.setup: radix ON (SGLANG_DS_RADIX_OVERRIDE=1), score_capture + selection_capture; COLD (fresh) then WARM (identical prompt, cached_tokens=6080); compare cold-vs-warm absorbed scores at the flipped logical positions (cold top-2048 XOR warm)
Q2_score_trace.captured_score_dtype: bf16 (the bf16-authoritative reduced view top-k consumed; dumped upcast to fp32, lossless)

result_raw_rank0_cached_prefix.example_layer3: cold_cutoff_kth=0.004272 vs warm_cutoff_kth=0.004395; a cold-only pos scores 0.00409 (< warm cutoff -> dropped warm), a warm-only pos scores 0.00488 (> warm cutoff). Real membership change driven by the score perturbation straddling the cutoff.

Q2_score_trace.both_ranks_consistent: rank0 and rank4 produce identical numbers
Q2_score_trace.verdict: SCORES DIFFER at 98.6% of flips (17556 / 17802). The deltas are NOT epsilon — median |Δ|=0.057, p99=0.32, max=0.74, large relative to the per-layer cutoff. The top-k membership genuinely changed because the absorbed score itself differs cold-vs-warm. Only 246 (1.4%) flips are bit-identical (true ties). A deterministic tie-break would address only that 1.4% and is therefore NOT a fix.

Q3_localization.method: inference from Q1 + Q2 + R24 (no separate v_h capture run; the chain isolates it decisively)
Q3_localization.input_1_latent: R24-proven BIT-IDENTICAL in the cached prefix (cold vs warm fp8+scale SHA equal at all cached-prefix positions; 0 differing positions)
Q3_localization.input_2_reduce: Q1-proven DETERMINISTIC (two fresh requests through the same bf16 custom-AR sum-reduce -> bit-identical scores). Given identical pre-reduce partials the reduce output is identical, so the reduce is NOT the source.
Q3_localization.remaining_differing_input: v_h = the decode query hidden state (the other multiplicand), produced by the model forward UPSTREAM of DS selection. Warm attends over reloaded/cached KV pages; cold attends over freshly-prefilled KV. That attention-output numeric path differs cold-vs-warm and feeds the query into DS. It is OUTSIDE the DS selector.
Q3_localization.verdict: The score difference originates in the QUERY-side v_h from the cached-vs-fresh model forward (upstream of DS), NOT in the DS score reduce or a top-k tie.

FEASIBILITY_VERDICT.a_deterministic_tie_break: NOT VIABLE — viable only if scores are bit-identical at flips; Q2 shows 98.6% of flips have genuinely DIFFERING scores. A tie-break fixes at most the 1.4% true-tie flips.
FEASIBILITY_VERDICT.b_reduce_order_pin: NOT APPLICABLE / NOT THE FIX — viable only if scores differ but v_h is identical; Q1 proves the reduce is already deterministic, so there is no reduce-order non-determinism to pin. The differing input is v_h, not the reduce.
FEASIBILITY_VERDICT.c_not_DS_fixable: THIS IS THE ANSWER — the divergence is the v_h / model-forward numerics from cached-vs-fresh attention, upstream of DS selection. It cannot be fixed inside the DS selector. The DS selection is already a deterministic, bit-exact function of its inputs (Q1); it faithfully reflects a query that legitimately differs between the cached-decode and fresh-decode forward.

bottom_line: A DS-side determinism fix is NOT viable. The cold/warm top-2048 divergence is not a DS selection bug and not a tie-break/reduce-order problem; it is the upstream model-forward producing a (slightly) different decode query v_h when the prefix is served from radix-cached KV vs freshly prefilled KV. DS selection is provably deterministic given its inputs (Q1) and consumes a byte-identical latent (R24); the only differing input is the query, which is outside DS authority.
